listBibl.bibl: Felix Liebermann, Die Gesetze der Angelsachsen, vol. 1 (Halle: Niemeyer, 1903), p. 625

An English crib of the Latin text, semi-literal, made for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model (LLM) made by Anthropic. It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: Ps Cn for 27.2
div.ab: Uulpes et lupi nec foreste nec ueneris habentur, et proinde eorum interfectio nulli emendationi subiacet; si tamen infra limites occiduntur, fractio sit regalis chacee et mitius emendetur.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 625 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: Foxes and wolves are held to be neither of the forest nor of venison, and therefore their killing is subject to no compensation; if however they are killed within the bounds, let it be a breach of the royal chase, and let it be compensated more mildly.
